One hotel night near Tokyo Disney? The right night depends on the hotel type: Disney hotel guests' early entry never works on the day they check in. Here's how we'd book it 👇

💴 The price gap surprised us. Take a guess, then look 👉 https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-disney-hotel-night-before-or-after

We read Tokyo Disney Resort's own rules and priced the same December nights at Maihama and in central Tokyo, for 2 adults and a 6-year-old.

🏰 THREE WAYS TO DO IT

1️⃣ Disney hotel? Book the night BEFORE. Happy Entry lets guests into Tokyo Disneyland 15 minutes early on every day of the stay except check-in day. Night after = no early entry on your park day.

2️⃣ Official Hotel like the Hilton or Sheraton? Book the night AFTER. Their official benefits list a free shuttle and baggage help, but no early entry. The park closed at 21:00 on our sample date, and a tired child is one monorail ride (about 13 minutes round the loop, ¥150 for a child) and a free shuttle bus from bed.

3️⃣ Already in Tokyo? You might keep your room. Hatchobori, the first Keiyo Line stop after Tokyo Station, had family rooms at ¥39,600 and ¥37,950 on Booking.com, against ¥43,000 and ¥40,000 at the Sheraton. Not much saved, but no repacking.

✅ OUR TAKE

Match the night to the hotel, not to habit. Disney hotel: night before. Official Hotel: night after. Keiyo Line base within a few thousand yen: stay put.

There's something lovely about walking out at closing time and being back at the hotel soon after, with the little one still humming the parade songs.

Night before or night after: which would you pick? 👇
